summary: Conservation is the backbone: Suriname states forest-cover commitments at both at least 90% and 93%, compared with 97.1% forest in the 2022 land-cover context. It also aims to conserve 30% of inland water and marine/coastal areas, raise forest-and-wetland protection to 17% of terrestrial area by 2030, and legally protect 3.5 million hectares by Q3 2030. Restoration and mixed land-restoration headlines are 50,000 hectares of degraded-land reforestation by 2035, 20,000 hectares of agricultural/pastoral land under active restoration, and 5,000 hectares of mangrove/coastal restoration. Agriculture targets include CSA on 60% of active farmland by 2035, agroforestry on 25,000 hectares, methane-reducing irrigation on more than 50% of rice cultivation, and a 25% post-harvest-loss reduction. In scale, 50,000 hectares equals about 0.35% of current forest cover, while 25,000 hectares of agroforestry equals about 32% of currently mapped agriculture. Mixed production pledges seek certification of at least 30% of productive forests.
